NONE: B2 a particular time, especially when something happens or has happened
（尤指某事發生的）時刻，時候
B1 a special or formal event
特殊場合；重大活動；盛會
› formal an opportunity or reason for doing something or for something to happen
時機，機會；原因，理由
C2 sometimes, but not often
有時；偶爾，間或
› to cause something
造成，引起；惹起

example: We met on several occasions to discuss the issue.
我們幾次會面討論這個問題。
I've heard him be rude to her on a number of occasions.
我有好幾次聽到他對她說話很粗魯。
I seem to remember that on that occasion he was with his wife.
我好像記得那一次他和她的妻子在一起。
Sara's party was quite an occasion - there were over a hundred people there.
薩拉的聚會真是一次盛會——有一百多人蔘加。
At the wedding he sang a song specially written for the occasion.
婚禮上，他演唱了一首專門為這次婚禮創作的歌曲。
I have a suit but I only wear it on special occasions.
我有一套西服，不過我只在特殊的場合才穿。
The coronation of a new king is, of course, a historic occasion.
新國王的加冕典禮當然是一個歷史性事件。
Congratulations on the occasion of your wedding anniversary.
在你們結婚紀念日之際謹致祝賀。
The 200th anniversary of Mozart's death was the occasion for hundreds of special films, books and concerts.
為紀念莫札特逝世200周年，出現了數以百計的專題電影、書籍及音樂會。
An occasion may arise when you can use your knowledge of French.
可能有機會讓你用用法語。
The bride took/used the occasion to make a short speech.
新娘利用這個機會簡短地講了幾句。
He has, on occasion, made a small mistake.
他有時犯點小錯誤。
Her refusal occasioned a lot of trouble.
她的拒絕引出許多麻煩。
[ + two objects ] The case occasioned the authorities a lot of worry/The authorities were occasioned a lot of worry by the case.
這個案子給當局惹來很多煩惱。

NONE: C1 not happening or done often or regularly
偶爾的；不經常的

example: I play the occasional game of tennis.
我偶爾打打網球。
He has the occasional cigar after dinner.
他飯後偶爾抽支雪茄。

NONE: B2 sometimes but not often
偶爾，間或；有時

example: I see him occasionally in town.
我偶爾在城裡見到他。
Occasionally I'll have a piece of chocolate, but it's very rare.
有時我會吃塊巧克力，不過這種時候極少。

NONE: › relating to the occipital area (= the lower back part of the head)
枕部的

example: A scan of the girl's brain showed seizure activity in the temporal, parietal, and occipital lobes of the brain.
女孩大腦掃描顯示在大腦側面、頂部和枕部都有發作跡象。
the occipital bone
枕骨

NONE: › relating to the occipital region (= the lower back part of the head)
枕部的
› the back of the head
枕部
› to block something
使…阻塞

example: Veins can get occluded by blood clots.
血管會被凝血塊阻塞。

NONE: › a situation in the weather when a mass of cold air reaches warm air and pushes the warm air up off of the earth's surface
囚錮鋒（兩個鋒面相遇而形成的鋒面，尤指冷空氣將其前面的暖空氣抬高而形成的鋒面）

C or U: › medical [ C or U ] in medicine, something that blocks a tube or opening in the body, or when something is blocked or closed
栓塞；閉塞（醫學術語，管道或體內開口處的阻塞）

U: › medical [ U ] in dentistry, the way in which your upper and lower teeth meet

C: › environment [ C ] also occluded front a situation in the weather when two masses of air meet, especially when a mass of cold air reaches warm air and pushes the warm air up off the earth's surface
囚錮鋒（兩個鋒面相遇而形成的鋒面，尤指冷空氣將其前面的暖空氣抬高而形成的鋒面）

NONE: › relating to magical powers and activities, such as those of witchcraft and astrology
有魔力的，神秘的；玄妙的
› the study of magic or mysterious powers
玄學，神秘學

example: She claims to have occult powers, given to her by some mysterious spirit.
她聲稱擁有某一神秘精靈賜予的神秘魔力。

NONE: › someone's use of a room or building for the purposes of living or working
居住；佔用；佔據
› the number of things, such as rooms, that are being used, in relation to the total number available
使用率

example: The family's occupancy of the apartment lasted only six months.
這家人只在這套公寓裡住了6個月。
The price for a room is $158 per person per night, double/single occupancy (= two people/one person in each room).
房間的價格是每人每晚158美元，雙人或單人房。
Average occupancy at Florida hospitals is now 49 percent.
佛羅里達州醫院病床的平均使用率是49%。

NONE: › a person who lives or works in a room or building
居住者
› a person who is in a car, room, seat, place, or position
佔有人；佔用者

example: The previous occupants were an Italian family.
先前的居住者是一家義大利人。
One of the occupants of the car was slightly injured.
有一位乘車者受了輕傷。

C: C1 [ C ] a regular activity or hobby

U: C2 [ U ] a situation in which an army or group of people moves into and takes control of a place

example: In the space marked "occupation" she wrote "police officer".
在「職業」一欄裡她寫了「員警」。
It seems to me his favourite occupation is eating.
在我看來，他最喜愛的消遣就是吃。
the Italian occupation of Ethiopia
義大利對埃塞俄比亞的侵佔

NONE: › relating to or caused by your job
職業的，工作的；由職業引起的

example: Back problems are an occupational hazard (= a risk that you take in a job) for any desk-bound office worker.
在辦公室伏案工作的人容易患背部疾病。
an occupational disease
職業病

NONE: › a way of treating mentally or physically ill people by getting them to do special activities
職業療法；職能治療
› An occupied place is being controlled by an army or group of people that has moved into it.
有人居住的；被佔領的，被侵佔的
› being used by someone; with someone in it
使用中的，有人使用的
› busy or interested
忙於；感興趣的

example: She spent two years in occupied Paris (= Paris when it was under foreign control) during the war.
戰爭期間她在淪陷的巴黎呆了兩年。
The bathroom at the back of the plane was occupied, so I waited.
飛機尾部的廁所有人使用，所以我等著。
At that time I was fully occupied taking care of my elderly mother.
那段時間我的時間都用來照顧我年邁的母親了。
All the new toys kept the kids occupied for hours.
這些新玩具讓孩子們興致勃勃地玩了好幾個小時。

C: › [ C ] UK someone who lives or works in a particular room, building, or piece of land, or someone who is using it

C usually plural: › [ C usually plural ] someone who has moved into a place and taken control of it

example: The envelope was simply addressed to "The Occupier".
信封上只寫著「住戶收」。
The occupiers were driven out after fierce street fighting.
在慘烈的巷戰之後，佔領軍被趕了出去。

T: B2 to fill, exist in, or use a place or period of time
佔有，佔用，佔據（空間或時間）
B2 to keep someone busy or interested
使（某人）忙於；使（某人）感興趣
C1 (of an army or group of people) to move into and take control and/or possession of a place

example: The rest of the time was occupied with writing a report.
剩下的時間用來寫了份報告。
The house hasn't been occupied (= lived in) by anyone for a few months.
這幢房子已經有幾個月沒人住了。
formal A large picture of the battle of Waterloo occupied the space above the fireplace.
一幅描繪滑鐵盧戰役的巨幅畫作佔據了壁爐上方的空間。
On long journeys I occupy myself with solving maths puzzles.
長途旅行時，我用解數學難題來打發時間。
Troops quickly occupied the city.
軍隊很快佔領了城市。
Protesting students occupied the university office for two weeks.
抗議的學生佔領大學辦公樓達兩個星期。
the occupying forces
佔領軍

I: B2 [ I ] (especially of accidents and other unexpected events) to happen
（尤指事故及其他意外事件）發生

I + adv/prep: › [ I + adv/prep ] to exist or be present in, among, etc.

example: An accident involving over ten vehicles has occurred in the east-bound lane.
在東向車道上發生了一起涉及十多輛汽車的交通事故。
If any of these symptoms occur while you are taking the medication, consult your doctor immediately.
服藥期間如果產生了這些癥狀中的任何一種，要立即就醫。
Violence of some type seems to occur in every society.
每個社會似乎都會存在某種形式的暴力。
Minerals occur naturally in the earth's crust.
礦物自然存在於地殼中。

NONE: › If a thought or idea occurs to you, it comes into your mind.
（某人）想到，（想法或主意）出現在（某人）頭腦中

example: The thought did occur to me.
我確實冒出了這個念頭。
[ + that ] It never even occurred to us that he hadn't been invited.
我們壓根兒沒想到他未被邀請。
Does it ever occur to you that I might want to be on my own sometimes?
你難道從沒想過有時候我或許喜歡獨處？

U: C1 [ U ] the fact of something existing, or how much of it exists

example: Street-fights are an everyday occurrence in this area of the city.
在該市的這一地區，街頭鬥毆每天都會發生。
The study compares the occurrence of heart disease in various countries.
該項研究比較了不同國家心臟病的發病率。
